draft.title: Development in infancy and early childhood
card: Infancy is the first year or so of life. Early childhood is the years after that, up to about school age. Development is very rapid in both.
Physical
growth in size and in movement skills. A baby learns to hold up its head, then to sit, crawl, walk and later to run and use a pencil.
Social and emotional

social development is learning to relate to others, such as playing with other children. Emotional development is learning to express and manage feelings, such as showing joy or calming down with help.
Intellectual
growth in thinking, language and memory. A baby babbles, then speaks single words, then puts words into sentences and asks questions.
draft.remember: In the early years, a child grows quickly in body, relationships, feelings and thinking.

a.q: A two-year-old starts joining words into short sentences such as "want more milk". Which type of development is this?
opts: Intellectual development
Physical development
Social development
Emotional development
a.why: Learning language is a growth in thinking and communication, so it is intellectual development. Social development is tempting because talking happens with other people, but the card places language under intellectual growth.
a.clue: Think about thinking, language and memory.

b.q: Tom, aged 4, used to cry loudly when his dad left him at kindergarten. Now he waves goodbye and settles with a teacher's help. What development does this show?
opts: Emotional, as he is managing his feelings
Physical, as he is becoming stronger and taller
Intellectual, as he is learning new words
Physical, as he can now walk into the room alone
b.why: Tom is managing his feelings about separating from his dad, which is emotional development. Physical development is about body growth and movement, and nothing in the case describes that.
b.clue: What is Tom learning to do with his feelings?

b.best: Emotional, as he is managing his feelings

problems.detail: VCE Health and Human Development materials usually define infancy as birth to about 2 years, with early childhood from 2 to about 6 years. Calling infancy 'the first year or so of life' understates it and does not match the VCE lifespan stages.
The clue 'Think about thinking, language and memory' repeats the card's definition of intellectual development word for word, so it gives the answer away.
The clue 'What is Tom learning to do with his feelings?' points straight to the only option that mentions feelings, so it gives the answer away.
The right option is the only one about feelings, and two options are both 'Physical', so a student can pick the answer without understanding the idea.

opts: Intellectual development
Physical development
Social development
Emotional development
a.why: Learning to use language is growth in how the mind works, so it is intellectual development. Social development is tempting because talking happens with other people, but the card places language under intellectual growth.
a.clue: Is this a change in the body, in relationships, in feelings or in the mind?

b.q: Tom, aged 4, used to scream when his dad left him at kindergarten. Now he still feels sad, but he takes deep breaths and calms down with a teacher's help. What development does this show?
opts: Emotional, as he is learning to cope with being upset
Social, as he is learning to share and play with others
Intellectual, as he is learning to use new words
Physical, as he is growing stronger and taller
b.why: Tom is learning to manage his sadness when his dad leaves, which is emotional development. Social development is tempting because a teacher is involved, but nothing in the case shows him sharing or playing with others.
b.clue: Compare what Tom did before with what he does now.
